text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
English physician JAMES PARKINSON, who defined Parkinson's Disease, was born in 1775.
English soldier and pioneer of Ipswich in Queensland, GEORGE THORN, was born in 1806.
German pianist and conductor SIR CHARLES HALLE was born in 1819.
Founder of the 'Australian New Guard' (a patriotic group opposed to Communism) ERIC CAMPBELL, was born in 1893.
Australian author and journalist CYRIL PEARL was born in 1906.
American actor and singer JOEL GREY ("Cabaret") was born in 1932.
UK singer with 'Brotherhood Of Man' LEE SHERIDAN was born in 1949. Hits include "Save Your Kisses For Me" (1976), "United We Stand" (1970) and "Angelo" (1977).
**EVENTS**
1713 : France gave up Newfoundland and Gibraltar to
Britain.
1913 : French aviator GUSTAV HAMEL set a record by flying
the English Channel from Dunkirk to Dover and back in 90 minutes.
1919 : The International Labour Organisation was founded
in affiliation with the League Of Nations, to improve living and working standards.
1921 : Australian aviator BERT HINKLER made world history
by flying his AVRO non-stop from Sydney to his home town of Bundaberg on the Central Queensland Coast. The flight took 8 hours and 40 minutes.
1929 : The cartoon character POPEYE appeared for the
first time in a HEARST newspaper.
1934 : The first air mail service began between Australia
and New Zealand.
1935 : Dust storms threatened much of the United States,
especially the 'dust bowl' States including Kansas, Texas and Colorado, bringing calls for the United States Government to declare the region a Disaster Area.
1951 : World War Two General DOUGLAS MACARTHUR, who
accepted the Japanese surrender in Tokyo Bay in 1945, was stripped of his command by United States President HARRY TRUMAN following differences of opinion on American war policy.
1961 : American folk singer BOB DYLAN made his first live
appearance, opening for JOHN LEE HOOKER at a folk festival in Greenwich Village.
1961 : Alleged Nazi war criminal ADOLF EICHMANN appeared
in a Jerusalem Court on 15 charges, centered on his involvement in sending millions of Jews to their deaths during World War Two.
1977 : Black American singer and dancer JOSEPHINE BAKER,
who found recognition in France, died.
1984 : A Glasgow couple received a pleasant surprise,
after taking an old lamp to an auction at Christie's in London. The lamp's base was a 14th century Chinese porcelain vase, and it fetched close to a million dollars! (421,200 pounds).
1984 : "Advance Australia Fair" was proclaimed as the
official national anthem and green and gold were named as the national colours.
1989 : English soccer clubs were re-admitted to the
European Cup, following a ban imposed because of the behaviour of soccer hooligans.
1990 : Suspicious looking 'oil pipes' bound for Iraq were
seized by British Customs. It was feared the large pipes were set to become part of an Iraqi "supergun".
1994 : The United Nations ruled that anti-gay laws
proposed by the Tasmanian Government were in breach of international civil and political rights.
